claim: The ventilation control should implement a bio-inspired neural network that mimics the distributed decision-making process of stomatal guard cells
mechanism: The control system uses a multi-layer neural network with inputs from CO2 sensors, occupancy sensors, temperature sensors, and time of day. The network processes these inputs through hidden layers that represent the interconnected nature of guard cell signaling, outputting damper position commands. The network is trained on historical building performance data to optimize ventilation efficiency.
evidence: Neural networks have shown success in complex control applications
Stomatal regulation involves distributed cellular signaling networks
Machine learning approaches have improved HVAC performance in some studies
assumptions: Neural networks can effectively learn the complex relationships between building parameters
The distributed processing nature of neural networks can capture the emergent behavior of stomatal regulation
Sufficient training data is available to develop an accurate model
novelty_rationale: This hypothesis applies the principle of distributed, emergent decision-making from stomatal biology to building control, using neural networks to capture the complex, non-linear relationships between building parameters.
testability: The neural network controller can be implemented and tested by comparing its performance against the current system and alternative approaches, measuring energy consumption, CO2 levels, and comfort complaints over a 30-day period.
falsifier: If the neural network controller performs worse than simpler methods or fails to converge to an effective solution during training, the hypothesis would be falsified.
